response.markdown_report:
**Selected direction: supervision-controlled prefix truncation in NextItNet.** At 10% progress, a small training intervention with an explicit control offers the clearest next experiment.

Three starting insights motivate it. First, positive sampled-negative margins coexist with weak training-prefix catalog ranking. These measurements concern different candidate sets and cannot establish a sampling failure. Second, terminal-preserving permutations worsen ranks on measured prefixes. This supports order sensitivity, while sparse replacement support leaves recency conclusions unresolved. Third, qualitative feedback favors specific recent context. Histories do not establish current intent, ownership, or compatibility, so truncation remains a hypothesis about generalization.

Three literature insights refine the design. NextItNet supplies causal convolutional features and supervision across positions [1]. Cropping can therefore change both context and supervision unless targets are explicitly matched. Effective receptive fields can be smaller than theoretical bounds [2]. Removing structurally unreachable history is a useful null control, although this literature does not establish NextItNet-specific gains. Activation-patching research shows that conclusions depend on corruption and measurement choices [3]. This motivates multiple suffix lengths without treating sensitivity as causal user preference.

The framework separates three directions:

| Direction | Intervention | Main unresolved question |
|---|---|---|
| Context regularization | Remove older prefix items | Does restricted context improve validation? |
| Supervision control | Match targets and negatives | Is improvement attributable to context? |
| Measurement calibration | Preserve positions; test unreachable edits | Does the probe measure the intended change? |

Three candidate algorithms, scored originality/potential/difficulty:

- **Matched truncation: 4/7/3.** Originality: controlled integration (+), established augmentation (−). Potential: isolates a useful training choice (+), may discard useful history (−). Difficulty: input-only modification (+), supervision alignment needs care (−). Builds on [1,2].
- **Suffix-length curriculum: 3/6/4.** Originality: temporal schedule (+), familiar curriculum design (−). Potential: gradual adaptation (+), adds schedule sensitivity (−). Difficulty: simple scheduler (+), harder attribution (−). Builds on [1,2].
- **Paired suffix consistency: 5/6/5.** Originality: shared-network regularization (+), established consistency principle (−). Potential: stable representations (+), may suppress useful context dependence (−). Difficulty: shared checkpoint (+), extra forward pass and loss tuning (−). Inspired by [3].

Choose **matched truncation**. Compare full-context and truncated-context conditions using identical training endpoints, negatives, loss reductions, and updates. In treatment, retain full context with probability 0.5; otherwise retain a uniformly sampled suffix between half and all available items. Preserve tensor width and retained positions through left padding.

Train each condition separately with one NextItNet per category; never combine predictions. Keep inference on the original full context. Select solely through pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; report category changes and cost. No improvement has yet been measured.

idea.description: Evaluate stochastic removal of older prefix items in the supplied corrected NextItNet, using a full-context control with exactly matched supervised endpoints, negatives, loss normalization, and optimizer updates. Each experimental condition trains one independent model per category and serves one checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnostics support sensitivity to history ordering but provide insufficient evidence that recent context is underweighted. A controlled truncation experiment tests whether limiting older context improves validation ranking without attributing any improvement to an accidental change in target selection or supervision volume. Its limited implementation scope suits the reported 10% research progress.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve the corrected NextItNet backbone, architecture settings, optimizer, objective, and baseline inference window for the initial experiment. Compare two separate conditions: matched full context and matched stochastic suffix truncation. Do not fuse their scores or checkpoints. Each condition starts from the supplied cold start, without reading another trial or reusing trained weights.

Use the family-specific sample_batch to obtain aligned training examples. Select one valid supervised endpoint per sampled row using a deterministic training-only schedule, and construct its input solely from interactions through that endpoint. Its positive label must be the following training interaction; exclude the target occurrence and later input context. Both conditions use the identical endpoint schedule and sampled negative IDs. This endpoint-only supervision is a deliberate common change relative to dense baseline supervision; therefore compare treatment against its matched control, and report the corrected dense baseline separately if available. A difference against the dense baseline alone cannot isolate truncation.

For an endpoint with n available input items inside the baseline window, retain all n with probability 0.5. Otherwise choose k uniformly from ceil(n/2) through n and replace the oldest n-k occupied input positions with PAD. Keep tensor width, terminal position, retained-item positions and any baseline positional IDs unchanged. Do not repack retained tokens or introduce an untrained mask token. Rows with one input item remain unchanged. Supervise only the selected endpoint in both conditions; use the same positive/negative loss and reduction. Preserve the baseline sampler's exclusion rules using the original training history rather than the truncated input. Do not add unavailable historical items as negatives. If no valid endpoint exists, handle it identically in both conditions and record exclusions.

Generate augmentation choices with a separate seeded generator so they do not change endpoint sampling, negative sampling, initialization, or dropout streams. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Preserve all four routes: Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], single-GPU execution, original splits, trial-local artifacts and host accounting against 43,200 GPU-seconds. Run conditions only within the remaining budget; failed runs and diagnostics count too.

At inference, use the baseline full context with no stochastic cropping. Gather the maximum index whose item ID is nonzero, never count-1; handle empty histories explicitly using the supplied baseline policy. Keep the trained class, checkpoint configuration and embedded predictor writer identical across training and serving. Each category predictor loads exactly one checkpoint. No score fusion, auxiliary transition predictor, pretrained weights or external data are introduced.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), all ModelView interfaces, and the B x L loader contract. Keep log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items) compatible. Diagnostic margin probes may still evaluate valid dense positions but must label them as training diagnostics rather than the endpoint-only optimization objective. Return metrics and metric_definitions, with null plus a reason for unavailable quantities.

Before training, verify on synthetic mixed-length examples that endpoint labels and negatives match across conditions, retained positions do not move, future tokens cannot influence endpoint features, and maximum-nonpadding readout is correct. Test edits outside the computed receptive field as a null control only if the actual architecture has no additional information paths. Derive reachability from the actual supplied backbone rather than assuming a window or receptive span from an earlier inspiration.

Select models only using the unchanged pinned host validation procedure: 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42, aggregated equally across four categories. Report per-category results and macro differences without inventing uncertainty or claiming a seed-averaged effect from seed 42 alone. Preserve full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for the prescribed five real training users per category. Use public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps only; do not infer ownership, compatibility, review evidence or simulator traits.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch


def truncate_old_prefix(sequence, generator, full_probability=0.5):
    """Training augmentation; sequence contains only context through its endpoint."""
    result = sequence.clone()
    for row in range(sequence.shape[0]):
        occupied = torch.nonzero(sequence[row] != 0, as_tuple=False).flatten()
        n = occupied.numel()
        if n <= 1:
            continue
        if torch.rand((), generator=generator).item() < full_probability:
            continue
        minimum = (n + 1) // 2
        retained = int(torch.randint(minimum, n + 1, (), generator=generator))
        result[row, occupied[:n - retained]] = 0
    return result


def final_nonpadding(features, sequence):
    positions = torch.arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
    final = positions.expand_as(sequence).masked_fill(sequence == 0, -1).amax(dim=1)
    valid = final >= 0
    return features[valid, final[valid]], valid


# Host integration outline; preserve the supplied family-specific implementations.
# Run each condition independently, without checkpoint or prediction combination.
for condition in ('matched_full', 'matched_truncation'):
    for category in FOUR_FIXED_CATEGORIES:
        seed_training(42)
        model = corrected_nextitnet_cold_start(category)
        augmentation_rng = torch.Generator(device='cpu').manual_seed(42)
        for epoch in range(min(configured_epochs, 200)):
            for batch_index in range(200):
                batch = family_specific_sample_batch()
                # Shared deterministic schedule across conditions; no held-out data.
                sequence, positive, negative = endpoint_examples(batch, epoch, batch_index)
                # Keep all labels/negatives fixed; the input excludes future context.
                if condition == 'matched_truncation':
                    sequence = truncate_old_prefix(sequence, augmentation_rng)
                features, valid = final_nonpadding(model.log2feats(sequence), sequence)
                loss = unchanged_endpoint_loss(
                    model.predict_score(features, positive[valid]),
                    model.predict_score(features, negative[valid]))
                unchanged_optimizer_update(loss)
        save_one_category_checkpoint_and_consistent_predictor(model)
# Predictor uses the original full context and final-nonpadding readout.
# Host independently evaluates each condition; select by four-category macro HR@10.

originality.positive: Makes context removal testable through explicit endpoint, negative, position and update matching within NextItNet.
originality.negative: Suffix augmentation and matched experimental controls are established techniques; the contribution is methodological integration.

future_potential.positive: Provides a simple foundation for studying how accessible context interacts with autoregressive supervision across categories.
future_potential.negative: Older context may be useful, and the supplied diagnostics establish neither truncation benefits nor reliable prediction of validation gains.

code_difficulty.positive: Changes training inputs while preserving the backbone, scoring interface and inference architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct endpoint construction, independent random streams and matched loss reductions require careful integration with the unseen baseline.

related_work.title: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Introduces NextItNet's causal dilated convolutional sequence modeling.
Provides the autoregressive supervision setting underlying the proposed context-versus-supervision control.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed matched suffix augmentation improves this benchmark.
Its architecture must not substitute for inspecting the actual supplied implementation during host integration.

related_work.title: Understanding the Effective Receptive Field in Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
contributions: Distinguishes effective influence from theoretical convolutional receptive-field extent.
Motivates separating structural accessibility from measured sensitivity.
limitations: Provides general CNN evidence rather than NextItNet-specific recommendation results.
Does not justify assuming older interactions are unhelpful.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: Examines how corruption and measurement choices affect intervention conclusions.
Motivates explicit controls and cautious interpretation of sequence perturbations.
limitations: Studies language models; transfer to recommendation requires validation.
Does not provide evidence that suffix consistency or truncation improves HR@10.
